name: Bab-el-Mandeb
genZNote: The name literally means 'Gate of Grief' in Arabic — a fitting name for a strait this narrow carrying this much of the world's Europe-Asia trade.

sections.heading: 🚨 Location & What It Connects
bullets: A narrow strait between Djibouti/Eritrea (the Horn of Africa) to the west and Yemen (the Arabian Peninsula) to the east.
Connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and onward to the Arabian Sea/Indian Ocean.
The name is Arabic for 'Gate of Tears' or 'Gate of Grief', reflecting its historical reputation as a difficult, dangerous passage.

sections.heading: ⚓ Why It Matters
bullets: The southern gateway to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal — a major share of Europe-Asia shipping, including oil and container trade, passes through it.
Djibouti has become a significant hub near this chokepoint, hosting several countries' naval facilities because of the strait's strategic importance.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 India Connection
bullets: India's trade with Europe and parts of Africa via the Suez Canal route passes through Bab-el-Mandeb, making it relevant to India's western trade corridor alongside the Strait of Hormuz.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Bab-el-Mandeb is a narrow strait between the Horn of Africa and Yemen, linking the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean.
keyFacts: Connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden/Arabian Sea.
Name means 'Gate of Tears/Grief' in Arabic.
Key link in the Europe-Asia Suez Canal trade route.
commonConfusion: Bab-el-Mandeb and the Suez Canal are two separate points on the SAME overall Europe-Asia route — Bab-el-Mandeb is the southern strait, Suez is the northern canal.

highYieldFacts: Bab-el-Mandeb connects Red Sea ↔ Gulf of Aden ↔ Indian Ocean.
Between the Horn of Africa (Djibouti/Eritrea) and Yemen.
Southern 'gate' of the Red Sea/Suez Canal shipping route.
commonTraps: Don't mix up Bab-el-Mandeb (a natural strait) with the Suez Canal (a man-made canal) — they're different structures on the same route.
mustRemember: Bab-el-Mandeb = Red Sea's southern gateway; critical link for Europe-Asia trade via Suez.
